- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) or shows strong reversal signals, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion toward historical range (e.g., 65–75) after a spike, model tends to hold too high; adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; use sentiment lag (e.g., 3–5 day average) to smooth forecast adjustments.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with cycle phase; align forecast with sentiment trend direction, not absolute value.
